sources.title: NIH Grants Policy Statement, FY 2020
sources.applicability: NIH grants and cooperative agreements with budget periods beginning on or after 2019-10-01; prior NIHGPS versions remain applicable to earlier budget periods.
sources.bounded_rule: The Grants Management Officer named in the Notice of Award is responsible for business/non-programmatic award management and is the only NIH official authorized to obligate NIH to Federal fund expenditure or change award funding, duration, or terms.
sources.exact_holder_resolution_rule: Identify the award-specific GMO from the relevant Notice of Award before naming an individual formal obligation authority holder.
does_not_establish: award-specific decision chain without Notice of Award

sources.title: NOT-OD-15-087: Publication of the Revised NIH Grants Policy Statement (Rev. 3/31/2015)
sources.applicability: The March 31, 2015 NIHGPS applies to grants/cooperative agreements with budget periods beginning on or after 2014-12-26 and supersedes the October 2013 statement for those periods; October 2013 remains standard for budget periods 2013-10-01 through 2014-12-25.
sources.bounded_rule: Authority mapping for 2014-era awards must use the policy version applicable to the award budget period and cannot silently apply a later policy version.

sources.title: U.S. Constitution, Article II, Section 2, Clause 1
sources.applicability: Federal reprieves and pardons, except impeachment.
sources.bounded_rule: The constitutional power to grant reprieves and pardons for offenses against the United States is vested in the President.
does_not_establish: scope of a specific pardon instrument

sources.issuing_authority: United States Code / National Archives statutory framework
sources.title: 44 U.S.C. § 2911 — Disclosure requirement for official business conducted using non-official electronic messaging accounts
sources.applicability: Executive-agency officers and employees creating or sending Federal records through non-official electronic messaging accounts.
sources.bounded_rule: A covered officer or employee must copy an official account when creating/sending the record or forward a complete copy to an official account within 20 days.
does_not_establish: that a questioned communication was a Federal record
that a personal account was used

sources.title: 44 U.S.C. § 3106 — Unlawful removal, destruction of records
sources.applicability: Federal agency response to actual, impending, or threatened unlawful removal, deletion, erasure, or destruction of agency records.
sources.bounded_rule: The head of the Federal agency must notify the Archivist and, with the Archivist, initiate action through the Attorney General for recovery/redress when the statutory conditions are met.

sources.title: Records Management Guidance for Federal Employees
sources.applicability: Federal employees conducting agency business, including use of personal/nonofficial messaging accounts.
sources.bounded_rule: Federal records created or received on personal/nonofficial messaging systems must be copied to or forwarded to an official account consistent with 44 U.S.C. § 2911.
does_not_establish: record status of a specific message
compliance or noncompliance in a specific case

missing_primary_authority_sources.purpose: Resolve exact Grants Management Officer and award terms for EcoHealth/Wuhan and other named grant questions.
Resolve scope/date language and any request/advice chain without inferring it from questioning.
Separate advisory influence from formal school/business/lockdown authority for policy questions.
Resolve formal authority for CIA/ODNI/DHS special-access, clearance, and classified-program questions.

promotion_boundary: This registry maps formal authority sources only. It does not establish that any questioned event occurred, that any named actor exercised the authority, or that any motive/culpability/legal/publication finding is supported.
